newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: South African stock market closing report.

text.p: A spurt of late local buying of South African industrial stocks lifted the overall market to end just above overnight levels after a day of busy, but evenly-balanced trade.
"There was some good nibbling in industrials just before the close," a dealer said.
"It was largely local, fed by a bit of foreign selling."
Industrials had spent much of the day hugging Wednesday's finishing levels, but moving weaker around noon on a softer rand and worse-than-expected October PPI figure.
A 19-point fall on Wall Street was also seen making players wary.

The rand slipped over two cents during the day, falling below the 4.68 level against the dollar. The PPI figure registered a 1.3 percent rise to 8.3 percent -- above a consensus forecast of 7.9 percent.

At the close the industrial index was up 8.5 points to 7,977.1 helped by a 60 cent gain in FNB to 23 rand, a 100 cent rise in Sasol to 57.25 and a six cent increase in Iscor to 337 cents. SAB, however, slid 25 cents to 116 rand.
Traders said dealings had been active with over 600 million rand's worth of trade passing through the bourse.
"There is very good two-way business. Good volumes are going through for the first time in a long while," a trader said.
Gold shares finished a touch weaker as bullion continued to hover below the key $370 level. But shares moved off their earlier lows, propped up by the weaker rand.
"The rand helped to stave off some of the blood-letting on the mining and gold board," one dealer said.
The index ended down 5.8 points to 1,510.7. Vaal Reefs was down 500 cents to 324 rand, Kloof shed 45 cents to 36.30 rand and Dries lost 25 cents to 50.50 rand.
The overall market index added 4.4 points to 6,717.6.

Dealers said the market remained edgy on the rand with some direction being sought from Wall Street overnight. The trend, however, seemed higher amid perceptions that shares had in recent weeks been oversold.

On the equity futures market, near-month industrial contracts slid further in late trading after an initial weaker start on the rand. Golds were steady to weak, poised between an ailing bullion and rand.
The December industrial contract was last at 7,660/78 from 7,732, the gold contract at 1,050/65 from 1,065 and the all-share contract steady at 6,170.
